findings.message: Time Budget says 'About 70% of each topic session is hands-on practice', but the plan's own per-topic minutes give 67% (EF Core performance 20/30), 60% (Query optimization 15/25), 53% (AsNoTracking 8/15), 67% (N+1 queries 20/30), and 67% (Indexing 20/30), about 64% overall (83/130).
findings.fix: State the actual share (for example 'about two thirds overall, about half for AsNoTracking') or adjust the wording so it matches the topic breakdowns.

findings.message: The new allocation explanation (revision item P4) reserves revision and mock time 'within the 10-15% target', but neither requirements.md nor research/data.md states such a target, and the plan does not say where it comes from.
findings.fix: Label the 10-15% revision share as the planner's own heuristic (or a planning assumption) rather than as an external target.

findings.message: 'N+1 is the most common hidden EF performance bug and a frequent code-review interview task' is not in research/data.md, which only lists N+1 among the usual root causes and says lazy loading hides it.
findings.fix: Rephrase to what research supports, for example 'N+1 is one of the usual root causes of slow EF data access, and lazy loading hides it'.

optional_recommendations: The Day 2 'Observe' note says offset time grows with the page number while keyset stays flat, but the exercise fetches only page 2,000; timing two or three page numbers would make that observation measurable (the wording is copied from research, so this is optional).
Buffering versus streaming (ToListAsync versus AsAsyncEnumerable) remains an unresearched optional Middle+ talking point; the plan correctly gives no content for it.
